title: Isolate provisioning state for fast non-destructive network changes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Small networking changes (route table tags, subnet metadata, security group rules) trigger long-running Terraform plans and high-risk diffs because the monolithic VPC state contains hundreds of resources and cross-cutting lifecycle hooks. This increases PR review time, raises blast radius for infra changes, and slows engineering velocity.

Goal: Refactor Terraform infra to separate long-lived VPC control state from short-lived provisioning state so that routine, low-risk network edits can be applied via ephemeral workspaces with minimal plan time and without touching unrelated resources. Deliver a migration plan, CI gating, and an automated rollback strategy.

Scope:
- Introduce a 'vpc-control' workspace containing the canonical topology and rarely changed resources (peering, NAT gateways, account-level route tables).
- Introduce 'ephemeral-net-*' workspaces for day-to-day metadata and application-level networking (subnet tags, per-service SGs, local route additions).
- Update Terraform modules to export stable IDs and remove implicit cross-resource lifecycle dependencies where possible.
- Implement a lightweight state reconciler job and a 'preview-only' CI workflow for ephemeral changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Routine subnet metadata change plan time reduced by >= 60% in staging.
- No drift introduced in vpc-control workspace after ephemeral deploys (verified by automated checks).
- Migration runbook documented (Confluence link) and validated on non-prod org.
- CI enforces that changes touching control resources require explicit approval and a separate deploy pipeline.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: Discussed pattern with network reliability, infra platform, and SRE. Decided split workspaces approach is preferable to per-resource microstates due to operational overhead. Action: prototype ephemeral workspaces in staging.

2026-02-26 - Design notes uploaded: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/isolated-provisioning-state (contains diagrams, proposed workspace boundaries, module interface changes). Key decision: modules must expose stable 'resource_refs' outputs rather than relying on data lookups across workspaces.

2026-03-02 - Prototype complete in staging account. Measured plan durations: full-vpc plan: ~14m, ephemeral subnet change plan: ~2.8m (80% reduction). Observed edge case where aws_route table dependencies required explicit null_resource hooks to avoid accidental recreation. Documented workaround.

2026-03-05 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/12345 - refactor(module): split vpc control vs ephemeral workspaces + outputs. Includes migration script to move ~40 resources from shared state into vpc-control workspace (uses 'terraform state mv' automation).

2026-03-07 - Review feedback from Security on IAM scoping for ephemeral CI roles: tightened policy to only allow state list/read/apply on ephemeral prefixes. Updated PR with policy change and unit test for least-privilege assertions.

2026-03-09 - Testing: Ran migration script in staging; had one conflict when an EIP resource had a lifecycle ignore_changes on tags in the legacy module. Resolved by temporarily removing lifecycle in staging, performing state move, then reapplying lifecycle in the new module. Added this as a migration step in the runbook.

2026-03-11 - Rollout plan: phase 1 - opt-in workspace for a single non-prod org; phase 2 - run reconciler daily and blockful scans; phase 3 - roll to prod with one team at a time. Added canary checklist and automatic rollback script that re-applies the last known-good plan if reconciler detects unexpected drift after ephemeral apply.

2026-03-12 - Blockers: Waiting on Dedicated infra team to validate NAT gateway references across accounts (dependency: ENG-47699). Also need a short RFC from platform about naming conventions for ephemeral workspaces (assigned to PM).
